<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-settings/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via /api/settings/:namespace (route, a path literal in a comment in SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via /api/settings/:namespace (route, a path literal in a comment in SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), getMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService), getNamespace (symbol, a method of class SettingsService), /api/settings/:namespace (route, a path literal in a comment in SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /api/settings/:namespace (route, a path literal in a comment in SettingsService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-settings/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6182249c3278a60d07727b59afc291054521b4b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `383edca2f60f01ab08aa2643f4432d53766caa19` — the merge of head `de2998b32bdf4b5bca9375072018940ea2ce98c2` into base `b6182249c3278a60d07727b59afc291054521b4b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 383edca2f60f01ab08aa2643f4432d53766caa19 && git checkout 383edca2f60f01ab08aa2643f4432d53766caa19
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b6182249c3278a60d07727b59afc291054521b4b de2998b32bdf4b5bca9375072018940ea2ce98c2 && git checkout -B drift-repro b6182249c3278a60d07727b59afc291054521b4b && git merge --no-ff de2998b32bdf4b5bca9375072018940ea2ce98c2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6182249c3278a60d07727b59afc291054521b4b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b6182249c3278a60d07727b59afc291054521b4b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 契约复审 · CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER · PASS · 2026-11-06T06:39Z · #30823

Head-sha: de2998b32bdf4b5bca9375072018940ea2ce98c2

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix (non-blocking):**
1. The pre-bind window. A namespace whose every key is pinned now reaches `loadRowSets`, and with it `reportPreBindRead` (`settings-service.ts` :2131, :3588). Before this PR it returned before any store read. `settings-prebind-read-warning.test.ts` :404 pins silence for `get()` only, so `getNamespace` of a fully pinned namespace read in the window now logs one warning per namespace. That is arguably correct, because the entries beneath are answered from the fallback, but the choice is undocumented. Name it in the docblock at :2104 or in a test.
2. The same fully pinned case with a tenant or user key now calls `organizationReachOf` (:2128–2130), which throws on a failed read (:2286). So a namespace read that used to answer from env alone can now fail. This is the same thing any unpinned key already does, and it is rare.
3. The `locked` docblock prose in `packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts` (:805–809, :825–827) still drifts. That is outside this card's surface, so it is recorded here only.

**Confirmed (read in the code):**
- **Chain invariants.** The env entry is first and the only one with `effective: true` (:2094–2103). The fill beneath it runs only when the env value is non-null (:2104–2107), so the first non-null entry stays env. `withStoredBeneath` strips `effective` from every entry beneath (:4185–4191). Top-level `value`, `source`, `locked` and `lockedReason` are unchanged. `resolveKeyFromRows` never emits `env` and orders global, tenant, user, default (:2194–2235), so no scope is duplicated or misordered. A lock on a global row beneath stays on its own entry and does not take over the top-level lock (test :3052–3072).
- **Secrets, on every path.**
  - In process, a pinned secret's rows go through `storedSecretPresence` (:2140–2146, :4197–4200) and come out as the mask or null, never decrypted (the test asserts that `decrypt` is not called, :3089–3112).
  - REST GET passes the whole payload through `redactSecretValues` (`settings-routes.ts` :309), whose `maskResolved` masks every non-null chain entry (`settings-secret-redaction.ts` :88–97). The route test checks that the wire carries neither the stored plaintext nor the env plaintext (:971–974).
  - `snapshotOf`, `servedManifest` and `resetNamespaceRows` do not read the chain. The PUT answer is `get()`'s, which is env-only.
- **Tenancy.** A pinned key joins the same `pending` groups, so its rows load with the caller's user and organization reach (:2123–2133, :3612–3630). The user rung compares `user_id` to the caller (:2227). A test shows only user A's row, and that a caller naming nobody gets none (:3074–3087).
- **Cost.** Pins add no extra read: one grouped load either way (`settings-getmany.test.ts` :246–264 pins equal find counts).
- **Tests.** All three of the card's cases (:3024–3057), secret masking in process, the REST level (`settings-routes.test.ts` :927–998, including PUT null then GET), the null-coercion gap (:3114–3124), and env-only `get` / `getMany` (:3126–3131). The ablation counts match the cases each ablation would trip.
- **Contract.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: the served namespace read carries more. `Metadata-protocol: none`: `packages/spec` is untouched. AGENTS.md (about :1026–1028) gives `none` a `patch` changeset, so the `patch` level is right.
- **Docs.** `config-resolution.mdx` :265–276 and the README :37–41 match the code.

**Consumers checked:**
- The console reads the chain only for the effective entry, and only when the key is not locked (`ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsField.tsx` :142–167, :246). `workspaceTimezonePromptLogic.ts` :263–268 reads `source` only.
- No in-process `getNamespace` caller outside service-settings reads `cascadeChain`: service-sms, service-storage, plugin-email, plugin-auth, and the organizations membership gate.
- Every service-settings test that reads a pinned chain was updated: the one prior pin is at `settings-routes.test.ts` :617.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-06T06:40Z · #30823

Head-sha: de2998b32bdf4b5bca9375072018940ea2ce98c2

- **Shape:** 7 files, +388/−12: `settings-service.ts` (+100/−11), three test files, the README's "Env override" section, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`, and one `patch` changeset. Everything is inside claim 6677761672 and README amendment 6677849918. Not governed.
- **What it does:**
  - `getNamespace`, the read behind `GET /api/settings/:namespace`, lists the stored entries beneath an env pin in `cascadeChain`. The env entry stays first and effective, and the answer's `value`, `source` and `locked` are unchanged.
  - A secret beneath a pin shows the mask or null and is never decrypted.
  - That is what #30665 needs to offer "clear the saved value". It reads the namespace endpoint.
- **Contract review:** PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, record 6678895942 at this head, no must-fix. It confirmed the chain invariants of the schema docblock, secret masking on every path, the caller's tenancy on the rows beneath, and no consumer that misreads the new entries.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - `get()` and `getMany()` stay env-only. They are per-request hot paths, and the schema docblock already scopes the chain to the inspection path.
  - An env value that coerces to null keeps an env-only chain, which is named as a gap in the PR.
  - The changeset is `patch`: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes patch per AGENTS.md, and the review confirmed it.
- **Recorded, not blocking** (review should-fixes 1 and 2): a fully pinned namespace now reads the store. So in the pre-bind window it logs one warning per namespace, and its organization lookup can throw as any unpinned key's can. Name the warning choice in a docblock or a test on the next touch of this file.
- **Gates:** every check-run on this head has concluded: 50 distinct checks, the latest run of each 38 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure. Locally (dev report 6678794925): service-settings 70/70 files, 1216/1216 tests; typecheck 0; `dispatch-gates` 90 derived, 90 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, all exit 0; `pnpm lint` 0. Ablations A, B and C each turn the expected tests red.
- **Contract:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, both confirmed.
- **Landing:** ready, then auto-merge, through the relay. `Fixes #30823`, which unblocks #30665.
